How do I file an income tax return?

### The Basics

The IRS has several different forms that are used to file your income taxes. Some of the most common are:

- W-2
- 1095-B
- Schedule 2
- Schedule 4
- Form 360
- and more!

This can be a confusing area for newcomers because there are many different forms that exist, each with its own unique requirements. While I will attempt to include as much information about these forms as possible (some I do not have time to cover), this website is still focused on helping you find your way around the IRS.

The most common form for filing an income tax return is the W-2 Form, which is usually used to file forms that are not considered “scheduled” and thus not covered by Schedule 1. The W-2 form can be found [here](https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i508) in most states. If you have a copy of your W-2 or a link, then you may use the online version of the website to help you navigate the process.

#### Scheduling Forms

Some forms require that you file them in one of two ways. In some cases they are “scheduled” meaning that they are filed at a certain time, such as after you receive income taxes from your employer or on your own. The other case is when it is not considered scheduled and instead is filed with you before you receive any money.

The majority of forms will be categorized under the 1095-B category because they are also required to file after you receive an income tax return from your employer that was received with a Schedule 2 or Schedule 4. The primary exception is when a form requires that it be filed before you receive your income taxes. These forms will be categorized under the “other” category.

In most cases, however, both these categories will require that you file forms in two places: one at your employer and another at the IRS. This can result in a lot of confusion for newcomers because it is very common to have the same form listed twice but with different dates.

The 1095-B form is an important form as this is required to file after you receive income taxes from your employer. The form also requires that you file a certain number of forms that are considered “scheduled” before filing them. These forms are also not considered “scheduled.” This can be confusing for newcomers because there will often be two forms listed as being both scheduled and not-scheduled, which is not possible!

  - Search by employee
  - Search by date of return
  - Search by name of returnant

  - Click on the link to find your form.
- By checking your mail

- If you have a hard time finding your form by checking your mail.
  - First of all, make sure that your return is received. This can take anywhere from 2 days or more depending on where you live (usually in the USA, you may find it takes a week). You should also double check to see if you actually receive income taxes. Some states do not give them out until at least three months after they are due.
  - The second thing to do is look for a mail that is called “Form 8602.” It will list the forms that you have received and whether or not your form has been filed. Look for forms that are not listed as having been filed but instead the letter “N” that denotes that it was not filed. This generally means that there were issues with the income tax return. A good way to check this is to look at the date of the form and then see if your schedule form was filed on a later date than the form listed. If you do find one, then double check that it is in fact the form that you want or the form that was originally supposedly due.
- If all else fails (which I doubt)
  - You should be able to contact the IRS and have them forward you your forms and schedule form(s). It may be a good idea to look up the dates of your return and the date on which they were received by clicking on the form 8602 link. Also, look for your mail that lists all of your forms in order (sometimes it is called “Form 4819” or “Form 3519.”)
- If you are unable to find any of these, then you may be able to send an email to <EMAIL>. Make sure to include the form number and state as well. When I am a member of the police force, I often ask my fellow officers to do things.  But sometimes there are situations where the same request is asked of all the officers at once.  In these situations I want the officers to make their requests one by one in one stop (i.e., not a batch).

I might ask them to clear officer X, and that X do some work.  The first stop would be to ask all officers for an overview of the situation (which is not possible with a batch), the second should be to ask the officer to ask all other officers for confirmation.  After the third stop they could then make their request.

I might ask them to clear officer X and Y.   It makes sense that in this case they need to do it one by one.  I might have asked them to clear officer X and Y.  They should do it in the following sequence:  First, they should ask officer X for an overview of the situation.  Secondly they should confirm it with each other.  And then finally they should ask officer Y for confirmation.

I might ask officers to clear officer X and Y.   It also makes sense that in this case I need them to do their work one by one.   They need to do their work in sequence; they cannot do one thing at a time, then another.  When I say that I want an overview of the situation or confirmation from all officers in one stop, it means that my request is not available for use.

I might ask my officers to clear officers X and Y.   What section would be appropriate?  If it was under "clearance" then all officers would be required to confirm each others work.  However the confirmation requests would then need to be made at least one stop after the first one is completed (i.e., before the confirmation of the first officer).  But that is not what I want.

I need to ask my officers for a clearance.   It should be available in 10 seconds or less, and ideally only 5 or 6 seconds.  The reason why is that we all have to work together in the moment.  We can not do one thing at time and then another.  And if we can't do it fast enough after the first one ends, then I need to clear the whole lot of them at once.
